title: Seeking advice for Music provider plugins
author: OinkLikeAPig
selftext:
Hi fellow builders,

I’ve been lurking alot for a while and been doing a ton of projects over the past six months.  
I’ve found my thing to try to finish.

We played Hitster the board game a lot this summer, and we talked about how it could be even better and more fun.   
I made it all and its fairly done. I’ve done a Spotify integration but from what I understand there is some legal stuff to take care of. 

So here is my question, how complicated is it to make it public with the accept from Spotify, Apple Music etc.?  
Anyone with experience?

As in the board game, you use your own private subscription to play.

comments.author: -svde-
comments.body:
what exactly are you talking about here? what does the board game have to do with the spotify integration? is this being built into an app that is meant to supplement play? or is this a digital game that mimics a physical one, or a hybrid? what exactly are you worried about legally? and what are you hoping that the distros will accept (if it some sort of deep integration that requires api and dev tools, you may have to pay a lot of licensing fees depending on what you’re wanting to do)?

this is all far too vague to give a definitive answer.

replies.author: OinkLikeAPig
replies.body:
Sorry about that, I wrote it quite fast just before bed and thanks for taking the time to reply anyways.

Its a digital game, where for now everything connect through a browser. So all players connect with each device.

There is one Host who controls the game.

The Spotify flow is: host creates the game -> host connects to spotify with personal account -> the game connects to spotify when the songs are played from the hosts personal spotify account. 

Data is retrieved as well as info about artist, year, genre and more. 

From what I could read, making this commercial would require some sort of agreement with Spotify and the other providers.
